own_inferences: Lineup coverage can be operationalized as a binary indicator that an offensive five-man lineup contains at least one player classified as organizer, one as shaper, and one as terminal scorer.
Within-team variation arises from substitutions, injuries, and lineup experimentation, allowing a fixed-effects design.
Talent can be controlled via offensive RAPM or a composite box-score talent proxy estimated from prior seasons.

Separating coverage from the count of each role type requires including the number of organizers, shapers, and terminals as covariates, so the coverage coefficient captures the synergy of having all three.
The possession-level outcome (points scored) is natural and avoids aggregation loss.
uncertainties: Whether the role classifications (based on usage and residual structural influence) are stable and reliable when estimated from partial seasons.
Whether sufficient within-team variation exists (some teams may almost always or never have full coverage).
The sensitivity of the result to the chosen role thresholds (median usage, residual cut).
The potential for reverse causality: poor performance leading to substitution that changes coverage.
The appropriate clustering level for standard errors given the hierarchical data.

blocking_constraints.text: Coverage may have limited within-team variation if many teams always or never achieve full role coverage, reducing effective sample size.
Structural role assignments depend on noisy estimates of usage and residual influence, particularly for players with few minutes, inducing measurement error in the exposure.
Coaching substitution decisions may correlate coverage with game situation, opponent tactics, or rest status, all of which also affect offensive efficiency.

prior_work.summary: No prior study-family records were found. The project’s glossary defines the roles but contains no coverage-hypothesis tests.

risks.text: If full coverage is very common (>90% of possessions) or very rare (<10%), the comparison group is small and estimates will be imprecise.
Roles are derived from play-type initiation data and structural influence, both of which have measurement error. Misclassification could dilute or bias the coverage effect.
Lineups are not randomly assigned. Factors such as score differential, opponent defensive strength, rest days, and back-to-back games may confound the coverage–efficiency relationship.
Exploring alternative role definitions, coverage thresholds (e.g., >=2 of each), or outcome windows without pre-registration could produce false positives.
Using a full-season role classification for a game that occurred earlier in the same season leaks future information and could bias the estimate if roles change over time.

Within-team fixed-effects regressions effectively use only the variation within a team’s stints; the number of independent stint-level observations may be insufficient to detect a small synergy effect.

If role classifications are based on in-season performance, lineups with full coverage may be composed of players who are temporarily hot, leading to a spurious positive coverage estimate driven by regression to the mean.

design.estimand: The causal effect of offensive lineup full role coverage (binary: >=1 organizer, >=1 shaper, >=1 terminal) on points per possession (PPP), net of individual player talent and the counts of each role type.
design.unit: offensive possession (excluding possessions with fewer than five players or after a technical free throw, using play-by-play derived possession endpoints).
design.sample: NBA regular-season and playoff possessions from 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and the complete 2025-26 regular season (up to 2026-04-13), with garbage time excluded (score differential >=25 in the 4th quarter).
design.power: We will compute power using 2022-23 and 2023-24 data as a hold-out: estimate the within-team standard deviation of the coverage indicator and the residual standard deviation of PPP after controlling for player fixed effects and game state. Assuming a minimum detectable effect of 0.02 PPP and 90 team-seasons, we expect >80% power with two-sided alpha=0.05 if the intraclass correlation is moderate. If power is insufficient, we will pool multiple seasons or adopt a stint-level design.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects; five-player average offensive RAPM (estimated from prior seasons, e.g., 2020-21 through 2021-22 using ridge regression) to control for talent; separate counts of organizers, shapers, and terminals in the lineup (0–5 each) to isolate the synergy effect; opponent defensive efficiency rank (divided into quintiles); game period (1/2/3/4) and interaction with point differential; indicator for second night of back-to-back; possession start time (seconds into the game) as a continuous spline to capture fatigue effects.
design.falsification: 1. Permute structural role labels within each team-season 1000 times and verify that the treatment effect lies near the center of the null distribution. 2. Re-estimate the model using the same coverage definition to predict the opponent’s points on the same possession (i.e., defensive outcome), expecting a null result. 3. Restrict to lineups where the coverage indicator switched due to a substitution event and compare the adjacent possessions before and after the switch, a form of within-game difference-in-differences.
design.multiplicity: The primary analysis uses one pre-registered coverage definition (median-usage threshold, residual-influence sign as defined in the Structural Influence paper). Secondary analyses with alternative thresholds or role aggregation will be reported with Bonferroni-adjusted p-values and clearly labeled as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Two-sided test of the coverage indicator coefficient from a linear regression (OLS) with cluster-robust standard errors (clustered on game), alpha=0.05. Pre-register that we expect a positive coefficient if synergy exists. The test will be considered supported if the coefficient is significantly positive and the falsification tests pass.
design.data_version: NBA play-by-play and matchup data from the NBA stats API as of 2026-07-13; play-type classifier version frozen at v2026-07-13; role definitions computed from player-level initiations in the preceding season (for 2022-23, use 2021-22 data, etc.).

TOOL_RESULT glossary:
# Terminology used in the research questions

This glossary is given identically in every condition. It defines terms only and reports no results. Definitions follow the published papers (Structural Influence; Detecting Defensive Suppression) where they exist.

- **Possession, PPP:** a team's continuous spell with the ball; PPP is points per possession.
- **H1, H2:** first half (periods 1 and 2) and second half (periods 3 and 4) of a game. RS and PO: regular season and playoffs.
- **Play type:** the label assigned to each possession by the project's rule-based classifier from play-by-play events. Labels include PNR (pick-and-roll ball handler), DRIVE, CUT, SPOT_UP, PULL_UP, POST_UP, PUTBACK and TRANSITION. A play-type mix is a team's share of possessions in each play type.
- **Initiator, initiation:** the offensive player whose action starts the possession's play type (for example the cutter on a cut, the ball handler on a pick-and-roll). Initiation records are possession-level rows linking initiator, play type and points.
- **Inferrer:** the classifier step that infers a play type (for example a pick-and-roll) from play-by-play text when it is not recorded directly.
- **Suppression trigger:** a team, play type and game in which the team's PPP on that play type falls sharply from H1 to H2 under fixed minimum-attempt rules; read as the defense possibly taking the action away.
- **Continuation, counter:** after a trigger, continuation means the offense keeps running the triggered play type; a counter is a different play type run instead.
- **BEST, AVOID (counter tiers):** the strategy app's matchup-ranked counter recommendations after a trigger. BEST is the top-ranked counter play type for that matchup, AVOID the lowest-ranked.
- **Structural fingerprint:** a team's standardized pattern of how play types share initiators.
- **Structural influence (load, L):** how much a team's structural fingerprint changes when one player's initiations are removed. L_pre is that quantity measured from games before an absence.
- **Usage:** a player's share of team possessions he initiates or finishes.
- **Role categories (Structural Influence paper):** by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (structural influence beyond what usage predicts): Primary Organizer (high usage, positive residual), Shaper (low usage, positive residual), Terminal Scorer (high usage, residual at or below zero), Role Occupant or Specialist (low usage, residual at or below zero).
- **Connector:** a structural-role label used in later studies for players whose presence links teammates' play types; the exact rule varied between studies.
- **Hub:** a high-structural-influence player around whom a team's initiations are organized.
- **Absence spell:** a run of consecutive games a player misses (the main studies used at least 15).
- **Displacement (D_real):** how far teammates' play-type mix moves during an absence spell relative to before it (one minus the cosine similarity of the two mixes).
- **Mover, decoy:** a mover is a player who changed teams between seasons; decoys are comparison players used as placebo matches for a mover.
- **Stint:** an interval of play with the same ten players on the court.
- **Garbage time:** late-game possessions with a lopsided score, usually excluded.

The phrase "Lineup coverage varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves." suggests they want to test whether lineup coverage (the presence of these role types) has a causal effect on some outcome, controlling for player talent and other factors. Possibly they want to see if the effect of coverage is distinct from the sum of individual talents (so a synergy effect). The research concepts include within-team variation, talent control.

Given no historical evidence, we need to reason from first principles using the available data. We have possession-level data, play-by-play, matchups, box-score. We can assign structural roles to players using the project's methodology (usage and structural influence, etc.). The roles are defined at the player level (over a season or a span). Then for each possession or stint, we can determine whether the offensive lineup includes at least one of each role (organizer, shaper, terminal). The coverage could be binary (>=1 of each) or maybe a count. The question "Lineup coverage ... varies within team" means that within a team across different stints/possessions, coverage does vary because of substitution rotations, injuries, etc. So we have within-team variation to exploit.

Separable from talent/counts: We need to control for a composite measure of the players' talent (like estimated RAPM, plus-minus, box-score metrics) and also perhaps the count of players of each role separately (maybe just having more organizers is beneficial regardless of coverage). So we need to isolate the effect of having the full complement of roles beyond the sum of individual talents or the count of each role.

Talent control behaves: Probably meaning that when we include talent controls, the estimated coverage effect is stable (not collinear), and we can interpret it.

Thus the testing approach: For each possession (or stint) with a given offensive lineup, compute outcome (points scored on that possession, or whether the possession is efficient, or net rating), compute coverage binary (1 if at least one organizer, one shaper, one terminal in the lineup, else 0). Control for the average talent of the five players (sum of their offensive RPM or something), and maybe also control for the count of each role separately (so that coverage captures the marginal effect of having at least one of each beyond just having many high-talent players). Use within-team variation via team fixed effects or team-season fixed effects. But there are potential confounders: lineups are not randomly assigned; coaches choose lineups based on opponent, game situation, rest, etc. So we need to control for game situation (score differential, period, time remaining, maybe garbage time excluded), opponent defensive strength (perhaps opponent fixed effects or opponent defensive rating), and maybe the presence of specific players that are correlated with coverage. EXPOSURE_SPARSITY: Some teams might rarely lack coverage (always have all three roles) or rarely have it, so variation might be low. MEASURE_RELIABILITY: Role assignments (organizer, shaper, terminal) depend on structural influence and usage thresholds; these could be noisy, especially if estimated from limited games. LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD: Need to ensure that role assignments are based on data up to the date of the game to avoid lookahead bias if using full-season roles. RTM_SELECTION: If roles are defined using performance metrics, lineups with certain roles might be composed of players who are hot or cold, leading to regression to the mean. CONFOUNDING: Coaching decisions might systematically place certain role combinations against tougher defenses, or when trailing, etc. We need to control for these. MULTIPLE_TESTING: If testing across many outcome definitions, need to adjust. BASE_RATE: Coverage might be very common, so the comparison group (lineups without coverage) is small, leading to low power. MECHANICAL_FLOOR: With possession-level outcomes, many possessions result in 0 points, but that's okay as we can use point total.

Design: estimand: The causal effect of having a lineup with at least one organizer, one shaper, and one terminal on offensive points per possession (PPP) relative to lineups lacking full coverage, controlling for team talent and game context.

unit: possession (or stint). Sample: NBA regular season and playoff possessions from 2022-23 through 2025-26, excluding garbage time (score differential >=25 in 4th quarter, or similar), using offensive lineups with five players on the floor.

Power: We will conduct a power analysis using within-team variation in coverage from 2022-23 and 2023-24 season to estimate the variance of the coverage indicator and the residual variance of PPP after controlling for player fixed effects and game state; assuming minimum detectable effect size of 0.02 PPP (roughly 2 points per 100 possessions) and intraclass correlation from team-season, we expect >80% power with the available 420k possessions.

Controls: Fixed effects for team-season, offensive player (or a composite talent metric like offensive RAPM estimated from prior data), opponent defensive efficiency rank for the game, game period, point differential, and seconds remaining in shot clock (if available); also control for the counts of each role type in the lineup separately to isolate the coverage synergy.

Falsification: repeat the analysis using placebo roles (random permutation of role labels within team-season) and check that estimated coverage effect is null; also test whether coverage predicts defensive outcomes, which should be zero if coverage only affects offense via synergy.

Multiplicity: single primary outcome (offensive PPP) and single coverage definition pre-registered; exploratory analysis of alternative role definitions will be reported with adjusted p-values.

Decision rule: coverage effect estimate with cluster-robust standard errors (clustering on team-season or game) and two-sided test at alpha=0.05; pre-registered hypothesis of positive effect.
